mainTopic: The stages of the decrees on ארץ העמים, and why the Rabbis decreed טומאה on glass vessels
overview: The גמרא works out how the decree of טומאה on ארץ העמים grew over time. It first suggests that יוסי בן יועזר ויוסי בן יוחנן already required burning תרומה that touched a clump of foreign earth. A statement of אילפא shows that only hands began at the level of burning, so the timeline is rebuilt to start with תלויה. Then a משנה listing six doubts for which תרומה is burned, together with עולא's statement that these were enacted at אושא, shows that the burning came much later. So the גמרא settles on three stages. First the clump causes תלויה. Next, רבנן דשמונים שנה make both the clump and the air cause תלויה. Finally, at אושא, the clump is raised to burning. The גמרא then turns to the decree on glass vessels. ריש לקיש explains that glass is treated like earthenware because it is made from sand. A משנה about immersing glass is answered as a case of lead-sealed glass, following רבי מאיר. The amud ends as a new challenge to the earthenware comparison begins, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: A new proposal for the two stages of the decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the first decree burned תרומה that touched a clump of foreign earth and said nothing about the air. Later, רבנן דשמונים שנה added that תרומה entering the air of ארץ העמים is held in abeyance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they (יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יוחנן) came and decreed that a clump of earth causes burning, and that the air causes nothing. Then the Sages of the eighty years came and decreed that the air causes the תרומה to be held in abeyance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is offering a new explanation of why two separate groups had to decree about ארץ העמים. It does this by giving each group a different piece of the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the earlier suggestion has been dropped. Here the first group already reaches the strictest level, burning, but only for direct contact with a clump of earth. The later group adds a milder rule, תלויה, for the air space. So each group decreed something new, and the decrees do not overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: A clump of earth (here, earth of ארץ העמים)
The air space of ארץ העמים
To burn: the תרומה is treated as definitely impure and must be burned
To hold in abeyance: the תרומה may not be eaten, but it is not burned either
The Sages of the final eighty years before the חורבן
Lands outside ארץ ישראל, which the חכמים declared impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. 'לשרוף' means the תרומה is burned. 'לתלות' means it is only put on hold: it is not eaten and not burned. The whole sugya depends on keeping these two levels apart.

phrases.english: Rather: they came and decreed
phrases.notes: 'They' refers to יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יוחנן.

phrases.english: on a clump of earth, to burn
and on the air space, nothing at all,
and the Sages of the eighty years came
and decreed on the air space, to hold in abeyance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ גְּזוּר אַגּוּשָּׁא לִשְׂרוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier explanation of the two-stage decree, on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redistribution: each group decreed about a different object (the clump or the air).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both groups seemed to make the same decree on ארץ העמים, which would be redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first group decreed burning for the clump. The second group added תלויה for the air.

steps.title: Challenge from אילפא: only hands started with burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: could a decree really start right away at the level of burning? אילפא said that hands were unique in starting at burning, which implies that every other decree started at a milder level.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that one decree was for burning from the start? But אילפא said: 'Hands, the beginning of their decree was for burning!' This implies that it was hands whose decree started at burning, but anything else did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proposal from step 1 using a statement of אילפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 claimed that the very first decree on a clump of earth already called for burning. אילפא singled out hands as the case whose decree began at burning. That only makes sense if other decrees, like the one on foreign earth, began at a milder level. So step 1 cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say...?' An opening that questions what a claim implies
'But didn't [so-and-so] say...?' Introduces a source that contradicts the claim
Hands: the rabbinic decree making hands impure for תרומה
The original start of their decree
Anything else

phrases.english: Is that to say that one decree
was for burning [from the start]?
But didn't אילפא say:
Hands: the beginning of their decree was for burning!
It is hands whose decree began at burning,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is picking this up from the exact way אילפא worded it.

phrases.english: but anything else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דַּחֲדָא גְּזֵירְתָא הֲוָה לִשְׂרֵיפָה? וְהָאָמַר אִילְפָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first decree on the clump was already at the level of burning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אילפא's statement implies that only hands began at burning, so no other decree, including foreign earth, could have started there.

steps.title: Revised timeline: each stage rises one level
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rebuilds the timeline. First, the clump caused תלויה and the air caused nothing. Later, רבנן דשמונים שנה raised the clump to burning and the air to תלויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they came and decreed on a clump of earth to hold in abeyance, and on the air nothing. Then the Sages of the eighty years came and decreed on a clump of earth to burn, and on the air to hold in abeyance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a corrected order of the decrees that fits אילפא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first decree starts at the mild level, תלויה, so it does not clash with אילפא. The later Sages raised each item by one step: the clump went from תלויה to burning, and the air went from nothing to תלויה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the previous answer and offers a new one
They decreed

steps.whatToRemember: Timeline at this point. יוסי בן יועזר ויוסי בן יוחנן: clump = תלויה, air = nothing. רבנן דשמונים שנה: clump = burning, air = תלויה. Step 4 challenges this timeline, and step 8 revises it by moving the burning to אושא.

phrases.english: Rather: they came and decreed
on a clump of earth, to hold in abeyance
and on the air space, nothing at all,
and the Sages of the eighty years came
and decreed on a clump of earth, to burn
and on the air space, to hold in abeyance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ גְּזוּר אַגּוּשָּׁא לִתְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by replacing the timeline of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-sequencing: the decree started mild and became stricter, as אילפא's rule requires.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clump was decreed at burning from the very beginning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clump began at תלויה and was raised to burning by רבנן דשמונים שנה, who also added תלויה for the air.

steps.title: Still a problem: the burning decree was made at אושא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new difficulty: burning for foreign earth was decreed at אושא, long after the חורבן. So how can it be credited to רבנן דשמונים שנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, it was at אושא that they decreed this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the timeline from step 3. Its proof, a משנה, comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 credited the burning decree on a clump of foreign earth to the Sages of the last eighty years of the Temple. But the burning decree is linked to אושא, where the חכמים gathered after the חורבן. If burning was enacted only then, the timeline of step 3 is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And still': there remains a difficulty
אושא, the town where the חכמים made enactments after the חורבן

phrases.english: And still: it was at אושא that they decreed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the revised timeline of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבנן דשמונים שנה decreed burning for a clump of foreign earth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burning decree on foreign earth dates to אושא, after the חורבן, not to the last eighty years of the Temple.

steps.title: The משנה of six doubts for which תרומה is burned
steps.stepSummary: To support the challenge, the גמרא quotes a משנה listing six doubtful impurities for which תרומה is burned. One of them is earth from ארץ העמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: For six doubts we burn תרומה: the doubt of a בית הפרס; the doubt of earth coming from ארץ העמים; the doubt of the clothes of an עם הארץ; the doubt of found vessels; the doubt of spittle; and the doubt of human urine that is next to animal urine. For definite contact with them, even though their impurity is doubtful, we burn the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה as the basis for its challenge. The משנה rules that earth from ארץ העמים causes burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all six cases the contact with the תרומה is certain, but whether the item itself is impure is only a doubt. Even so, the חכמים required burning. Earth from ארץ העמים is on this list. The גמרא will tie this list to אושא, which would place the burning decree after the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubts: cases of uncertain impurity
A field where a grave was plowed up, scattering bones
A person who is not careful about purity laws
Definite contact with them
Doubt whether they themselves are impure

steps.confusionAlert: The doubt here is not whether the תרומה touched the item. That is certain. The doubt is whether the item itself is impure. Even so, the תרומה is burned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source that moves the burning decree on foreign earth to אושא, which reopens the question of what each earlier group actually decreed.

phrases.english: As we learned: for six doubts
we burn the תרומה:
for the doubt of a field with a plowed-up grave,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל סְפֵק עָפָר הַבָּא מֵאֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים,
phrases.english: and for the doubt of earth that comes from the land of the nations,
phrases.notes: This is the item that matters for the challenge.

phrases.english: and for the doubt of the clothes of an עם הארץ,
and for the doubt of vessels that are found,
and for the doubt of spittle,
and for the doubt of human urine
that is next to animal urine:
for definite contact with them
even with doubt about their impurity
we burn the תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: עַל שִׁשָּׁה סְפֵקוֹת שׂוֹרְפִין אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text behind the challenge of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That burning תרומה because of foreign earth is a decree linked to אושא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the 'six doubts' (שִׁשָּׁה סְפֵקוֹת), which lists earth from ארץ העמים among the cases where תרומה is burned.

steps.title: End of the quoted משנה: uncertain contact
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends with a dispute about uncertain contact with these six impurities. רבי יוסי says to burn the תרומה in a private domain. The חכמים say to hold it in abeyance in a private domain, and that it is pure in a public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even when it is uncertain whether there was contact, if it happened in a private domain, we burn. The Sages say: in a private domain we hold it in abeyance, and in a public domain it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is simply finishing the משנה it began quoting in the last step. The real point of the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said that תרומה is burned when it definitely touches one of these six. Now it adds a disagreement about cases where the contact itself is uncertain. רבי יוסי treats it strictly, like Torah-level impurity. The חכמים are more lenient because these impurities are only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about whether there was contact with them
Private domain
Public domain
Hold in abeyance (do not burn, do not eat)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
even for uncertain contact with them
in a private domain, one burns.
And the Sages say:
in a private domain, one holds it in abeyance;
in a public domain, they are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 5
steps.raayaObject: The claim that burning for foreign earth is part of the 'six doubts' משנה

steps.title: עולא dates the six doubts to אושא
steps.stepSummary: עולא says these six doubtful impurities were set at אושא. That means burning for foreign earth is a late decree, not one from רבנן דשמונים שנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: these six doubtful cases were instituted in אושא!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the challenge from step 4. The burning rule for foreign earth comes from אושא, so it cannot belong to the earlier Sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה alone only showed that foreign earth causes burning. עולא adds when that burning was decreed: at אושא, after the חורבן. This contradicts step 3, which credited the burning to רבנן דשמונים שנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Town where the Sanhedrin sat after the חורבן and issued enactments
They enacted or instituted

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
these six doubtful cases
were instituted in Usha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the dating that turns the משנה into a real contradiction
steps.raayaObject: Burning for foreign earth dates to אושא, not to רבנן דשמונים שנה

steps.title: A three-stage timeline for foreign earth and air
steps.stepSummary: The decree developed in three stages. First, the two יוסי's made the clump cause abeyance and the air cause nothing. Then רבנן דשמונים שנה made both cause abeyance. Finally, אושא raised the clump to burning and left the air at abeyance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they (the two יוסי's) came and decreed abeyance for a clump of earth and nothing for the air. רבנן דשמונים שנה came and decreed abeyance for both. Then at אושא they came and decreed burning for the clump, and the air stayed as it was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adding a third stage to the timeline. The burning is moved to אושא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 had two stages, with burning given to רבנן דשמונים שנה. Now רבנן דשמונים שנה only added the air at the level of abeyance, and the burning was added later at אושא. This also fits אילפא's rule from step 2, since every decree still started at a milder level.

keyTerms.meaning: A clump of earth
The air space (of foreign lands)
This one and that one, meaning both
It stays as it stood (no change)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages. The two יוסי's: clump causes abeyance, air causes nothing. רבנן דשמונים שנה: both cause abeyance. אושא: clump causes burning, air stays at abeyance.

phrases.english: Rather, they (the two Yosei's) came
and decreed abeyance for a clump of earth
and for the air, nothing at all;
then the Rabbis of the eighty years came
and decreed abeyance for both;
then at Usha they came
and decreed burning for the clump,
and for the air, it stays as it stood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ גְּזוּר אַגּוּשָּׁא לִתְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dating challenge of steps 4-7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן דשמונים שנה decreed burning for the clump
steps.terutzMaskana: Burning for the clump came only at אושא; רבנן דשמונים שנה added abeyance for the air

steps.title: Why did the Rabbis decree impurity on glass?
steps.stepSummary: Under Torah law, glass vessels cannot become impure. The גמרא asks why the Rabbis decreed impurity on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Glass vessels — what is the reason the Rabbis decreed impurity on them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the decree on glass vessels, another of the earlier decrees. It is asking for the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Glass is not one of the materials the Torah lists as able to become impure. So there must be a rabbinic reason for treating it as able to become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Glass vessels
What is the reason?
They decreed

phrases.english: Glass vessels:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזוּר בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Rabbis decreed impurity on them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזוּר בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a different one of the decrees
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the rabbinic impurity of glass

steps.title: Glass is made of sand, so it is like earthenware
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoted by רבי יוחנן, explains that glass comes from sand. So the Rabbis gave it the status of earthenware vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of ריש לקיש: since glass vessels begin as sand, the Rabbis equated them with earthenware vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Glass and earthenware both come from the ground, so glass was treated like earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earthenware can become impure under Torah law. Since glass shares its origin in earth, the Rabbis gave glass the same status. The next step tests how far this comparison goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of their making (their raw material)
Sand
Earthenware vessels
They made them equal

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said that Reish Lakish said:
since their making begins from sand,
the Rabbis equated them with earthenware vessels.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Glass is treated like earthenware because both come from earth

steps.title: But glass can be purified in a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: If glass is like earthenware, it should not be purifiable in a מקוה. Yet a משנה about things that block immersion lists pitch on glass vessels. That implies glass vessels are immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, they should have no purification in a מקוה. Why did we learn: 'These block immersion in vessels: pitch and myrrh on glass vessels'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's comparison. A משנה shows that glass behaves differently from earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earthenware can only be purified by breaking it; immersion does not help. The משנה worries about pitch blocking the water on glass, which only matters if immersing glass works. So glass seems to be purified like metal, not like earthenware.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (from now on, by your logic)
Ritual bath
Block or interpose (prevent water from reaching)
Pitch

phrases.english: But if so,
they should have no purification in a mikveh.
Why did we learn:
'And these block immersion in vessels:
pitch and myrrh on glass vessels'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה לֹא תְּהֵא לָהֶן טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's comparison of glass to earthenware
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Earthenware cannot be purified in a מקוה, but a משנה implies glass can be

steps.title: A special case: glass sealed with lead
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking of glass with holes that were sealed with lead. It follows רבי מאיר, who says an object takes the status of the material that holds it together. So the vessel is treated like metal and can be immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where they were perforated and he dripped lead into them. And this is רבי מאיר, who said: everything follows the reinforcing material.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by limiting the משנה to an unusual case. Normal glass is still like earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A glass vessel with a hole is useless, and the lead is what makes it work again. According to רבי מאיר, the whole vessel then takes on lead's status as a metal. Metal vessels are purified in a מקוה, which explains the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
They were perforated (got holes)
Lead
The material that holds it together or makes it usable

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
A case where they were perforated and he dripped lead into them.
And this follows Rabbi Meir,
who said: everything follows the reinforcing material.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that all glass vessels can be immersed
steps.terutzMaskana: Only lead-sealed glass, per רבי מאיר, takes metal status and can be immersed; ordinary glass is like earthenware

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר's view on lead-sealed glass
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that for glass vessels sealed with lead, רבי מאיר says they are impure and the חכמים say they are pure. This shows רבי מאיר treats such vessels by the lead's status.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: glass vessels that were perforated and he dripped lead into them — רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: רבי מאיר deems them impure and the חכמים deem them pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that רבי מאיר really holds this view about lead-sealed glass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the holed glass stays a broken vessel and cannot become impure. For רבי מאיר, the lead makes it a working metal vessel. A metal vessel can become impure, and it can also be purified in a מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it impure (able to become impure)
Rule it pure

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי מאיר 'מטמא' does not mean he is simply being strict. It means he treats the vessel as a real metal vessel. A metal vessel can become impure, and that same metal status lets it be purified in a מקוה.
steps.whatToRemember: Ordinary glass is like earthenware because it comes from sand. The משנה about immersing glass refers only to lead-sealed glass, following רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Glass vessels that were perforated
and he dripped lead into them:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Rabbi Meir deems them impure, and the Sages deem them pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the attribution to רבי מאיר in step 12
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר holds that lead-sealed glass takes the lead's status
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: Opening a new challenge to the earthenware comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge with 'אלא מעתה'. If glass is treated like earthenware, it should follow other earthenware rules too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, that glass vessels are treated like earthenware vessels,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next challenge. It takes the idea that glass is like earthenware and gets ready to show a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלא מעתה' means: if your answer is true, then something else should follow. The earlier answer was that glass is like earthenware because both come from sand. Now the גמרא will push this comparison further to see if it still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so / but now (according to what you said). A phrase that opens a challenge by taking the previous answer to its logical result.
Earthenware vessels. These are the vessels that glass was compared to.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full question yet. It only opens the challenge. The actual problem the גמרא wants to raise comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: But if that is so (that glass is like earthenware)
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא starts pushing back: if the last answer is right, look where it leads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 13 confirmed the answer about lead-sealed glass, the גמרא goes back to the basic comparison from step 10 (glass is like earthenware) and starts a new objection against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison from step 10 that the Rabbis gave glass vessels the status of earthenware vessels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If glass really has earthenware status, then all earthenware rules should apply to it. The גמרא is about to point to a rule that might not fit glass. The specific rule appears on the next amud.
